discovery: Prediction and discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting phases in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene

nominees.name: Allan H. MacDonald
nominees.affiliation: University of Texas at Austin, USA

subfield: Condensed matter physics: strongly correlated electrons and moire quantum materials
motivation: Bistritzer and MacDonald (2011) predicted that at a 'magic' twist angle the bands of bilayer graphene become nearly flat, so that interactions dominate kinetic energy. Jarillo-Herrero's group (2018) realized this, discovering correlated insulators and superconductivity tunable by a gate voltage in a single device. This created a new, clean and controllable platform for the central problem of correlated-electron physics: how strong interactions give rise to insulators, superconductivity, nematicity, orbital magnetism and intertwined orders. The field it opened has been durable and broad. Moire systems have since produced the quantum anomalous Hall effect, generalized Wigner crystals and fractional Chern insulators at zero field, which are now studied in hundreds of laboratories. Few recent developments have changed so fundamentally how our community poses and tests questions about strongly correlated quantum matter.
